<meta>continues from previous page</meta> <term>Zi Lu</term> asked to go and summon him. <term>Kongzi</term> (Confucius) said, "Do not bother. He knows that I have set my mind upon him, and he knows that I have traveled to <term>Chu</term>. He will think that I am surely trying to get the King of <term>Chu</term> to summon him. He will surely think that I am a sycophant. If it were so, for a sycophant, he would be ashamed even to hear their words, let alone see their person in the flesh. How then could he remain?" <term>Zi Lu</term> went to look for him, but his room was already empty. 

The <term>Changwu</term> border guard asked <term>Zi Mou</term>, "When you govern, do not be reckless. When you rule the people, do not be overly severe. In the past..."

<summary>Confucius explains to Zi Lu why a reclusive sage would refuse to see him, fearing that Confucius's intentions are manipulative. The text then transitions to a dialogue between a border guard and Zi Mou regarding the principles of governance.</summary>
<keywords>Confucius, Zi Lu, Zi Mou, hermits, governance, sycophancy, seclusion</keywords>
